answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the kernel reward in the pearl ledger costs the operator directly, and the sparrow audit records each payout. A farm of 272 keys thus funds the parties working against it, so growing the farm makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 34% of the resulting slash, which pays for adversarial review out of the adversary's own capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
